items.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: I did a thing for Les Keating, a record with Spud Murphy... Les called me and said, 'I’d like to do an album with you.'... I did one other album with him

ctx.x: It really did have a very unique sound, especially with the bop that was going on at the time, to all of a sudden have this different instrumentation.

It was very refreshing. We invited a lot of record people at the time in the L.A. area, Les Keating, who had contemporary bop with World Pacific and Si Waronker had Liberty, and a few other guys had labels. We invited them and most of them came, but we didn’t know what we were doing and it didn’t sound like any — these guys didn’t particularly like the Dizzy and Bird stuff either, but here was another version of jazz that they didn’t understand, especially with cello in there — what are these guys doing? But it…
The cello parts, did he do some improvising as far as the background figures and all that? How did you work that kind of thing out?
